definition.title: Tensorspine reference catalog
definition.summary: Logical primitives, named axes and precision roles that model documents pin by identity.
definition.description:
Every unit of this base is one file whose path reproduces its identity (§8.2). A **contract** declares what a primitive means and what follows from its arguments: ports and shapes, learned tensors, persistent state with its evolution law, logical cost and semantic partitions. An **axis** names a dimension so that shapes unify by identity rather than by position. A **precision role** bounds the storage types a tensor, activation or state component may take.

The catalog is an open vocabulary of closed elements: a new primitive is a new file, and an existing `{name, version}` never changes meaning. There is deliberately no catalog-wide version.

external_docs.title: Tensorspine Language Specification
external_docs.description: Normative authority on contract contents (§4) and identity (§8.2).

tags.name: sequence-operator
tags.summary: Communicates tokens along the sequence and therefore carries state (§4.1).
tags.description: Only a sequence operator carries state. Every other primitive is stateless: a runtime needs no allocation strategy for it beyond its parameters and activations.

tags.name: multimodal
tags.summary: Crosses a modality boundary: audio or vision into the token stream.

tags.name: parallel-residual
tags.summary: The residual is several parallel streams (§3.5): AltUp, hyper-connections.

definition.note: Catalogue of logical primitives, independent of any library: physical fusions, shards, quantizations and synthetic tensors are outside the contract vocabulary.
